policy: These entries record specific Human Design sources' gate-level organ, tissue, or hormonal correspondences. They are not established biology, assay interpretation, or evidence that a gate causes, measures, or predicts a hormone. Preserve each source and its wording; do not generalize one source's teaching to all Human Design lineages. Conflicting source attributions are retained separately and must not be summarized as lineage consensus.

targetConcept.label: Female reproductive system and hormone production

correspondences.claimText: Human Design App's Gate 6 article says Gate 6 is linked to the female reproductive system and hormone production. This is that source's correspondence, not an established physiological association.

sourceCitations.title: Gate 6 Human Design: The Gate of Friction and Emotional Awareness
sourceCitations.locator: Biological & Energetic Connection of Gate 6

limitations: This is an attribution to one contemporary Human Design source; it is not a universal or canonical lineage claim.
The cited source does not identify a specific hormone, assay, direction, dose, or validated gate-to-hormone mechanism.
It does not identify an individual's reproductive anatomy, hormone level, fertility, cycle phase, or health state.

sourceSystem.version: Gate 41.1 article accessed 2026-10-20

correspondences.claimText: In a reproduced Ra Uru Hu teaching on Gate 41.1, the Root is described as dealing with adrenaline. Metheus records this as a source-attributed Gate 41/Root teaching, not as evidence that Gate 41 regulates adrenaline.

sourceCitations.title: Gate 41 in Line 1 of Human Design (41.1 Reasonableness)
sourceCitations.locator: Ra Uru Hu on 41.1 Reasonableness

limitations: The source associates adrenaline with the Root center in a Gate 41.1 lecture context; it does not make adrenaline a measured gate-specific output.
This is a source-specific symbolic teaching, not a biomedical mechanism or consensus across Human Design lineages.
It does not estimate an individual's catecholamine level or stress response.
